concerns.text: T017a (timestamp alignment) and T017b (interpolation) are listed as separate tasks within the same file (preprocess.py) but T017b explicitly depends on the output of T017a (aligned timestamps) to identify 'null/missing values' correctly. However, the task list does not enforce this sequential dependency; they are presented as parallelizable or unordered items. T017b must strictly follow T017a to avoid processing misaligned data.

T028 (Statistical Validity Check) reads from 'data/processed/granger_results.csv', which is the output of T026 (Granger causality test). T027 (Sensitivity Analysis) also reads from the same file. The current list places T028 before T027, but both depend on T026. While T028 and T027 are independent of each other, the ordering implies T028 might run before T026 completes if executed strictly by list order. T026 must be explicitly marked as a prerequisite for both T027 and T028.

T029 (Report Generation) depends on the output of T025 (Correlation), T026 (Granger), T027 (Sensitivity), and T028 (Validity Check). The task list places T029 after T028, but does not explicitly state that it waits for T025, T026, and T027 to complete. If T025 or T027 are delayed or fail, T029 might attempt to generate a report with missing data. T029 must be ordered after the completion of all analysis tasks (T025-T028).

T001-T006 are marked [P] (parallel-safe). While creating directories and installing dependencies can technically run in parallel, T004 (Create venv) and T005 (Install dependencies) have a strict dependency: T005 must run inside the environment created by T004. Marking them as parallel-safe without a note about the venv activation context could lead to race conditions where T005 installs to the global environment instead of the new venv.
